extracted.intended_audience: journalists and consumers of health news; potential expert contributors and funders
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational standards and evaluative principles used by HealthNewsReview.org for assessing health care journalism, advertising, PR and other consumer-facing health messages, plus editorial independence and contributor-conflict rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help consumers critically analyze health care claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission is to improve the public dialogue about health care by helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HealthNewsReview.org evaluates health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers, and provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote shared decision-making with accurate, balanced, complete information
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good health information should present tradeoffs clearly so consumers can participate in shared decision-making; evaluations should check for accuracy, balance and completeness of those tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation — not medical advice or advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org is not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science, does not give medical advice, and is not an advocacy group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review efforts are limited to reviewing daily health care news stories, journal practices and health care advertising, PR and marketing messages; the site will not expand beyond its capabilities or take on roles that would require giving medical advice or advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from industry influence — no conflicted funding or advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org does not accept advertising, nor does it accept funding from any entity whose support would represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy is intended to ensure readers that content has not been influenced by commercial interests and that the site's analysis represents an honest effort to report the truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert contributor conflict-of-interest pledge
rubrics_metrics.description: All expert contributors pledge that they do not accept payments from drug or device companies or from any commercial entity whose support might represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit only independent experts to participate on the team to ensure objective, independent analysis of health care claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and vetting of external experts' financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting someone who’s not a member of the team, ask them about any financial interests they may have in the topic, and disclose those interests in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about outside experts’ financial interests is required when they are quoted so readers can assess potential bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize work within staff capacity; selection is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The site cannot review every story or promotional message due to a small editorial staff and a set budget; the volume of health care information is overwhelming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are asked to understand that not every item can be reviewed; this practical limitation shapes what is selected for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational provenance and model acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The website is modeled in large part on the Media Doctor Australia effort and acknowledges similar international projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging provenance and related projects situates evaluation criteria within a broader community of practice and establishes methodological lineage; this also signals that similar standards have been used elsewhere.
